code_quality.title: Split UnifiedBookingEngine.tsx (3,667 lines) into domain-focused modules
code_quality.description: The UnifiedBookingEngine.tsx component has grown to 3,667 lines and handles 6 different booking modes (slots, daily, dateRange, event, recurring, instant). This violates single responsibility principle and makes the code extremely difficult to maintain, test, and review.
code_quality.rationale: This monolithic component has multiple responsibilities: calendar/date selection logic for 6 booking modes, price calculation, form handling, booking submission, and 500+ lines of inline CSS. Functions like RecurringModeView (181 lines) and BookingConfirmStep (202 lines) exceed reasonable sizes. Deep nesting makes flow hard to follow.
code_quality.currentState: Single 3,667-line file handling all booking modes with inline CSS, nested sub-components, price calculations, and form logic
code_quality.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - each module should have one reason to change. Components over 500 lines are maintenance nightmares.
prerequisites: Create comprehensive tests for existing booking flows before refactoring
Document current behavior for each booking mode

code_quality.title: Extract duplicated ListingsFilterBar component into shared @xala/ds package
code_quality.description: The ListingsFilterBar component is nearly identically implemented in both apps/minside (687 lines) and apps/backoffice (682 lines). Both files share identical imports, props interface, CAPACITY_OPTIONS constant, and core logic for search debouncing, filter handling, and view mode changes.
code_quality.rationale: Code duplication leads to bugs when fixes are applied inconsistently. Currently any filter behavior change requires updating two files, increasing maintenance burden and risk of divergence. The components share 90%+ identical code.
code_quality.currentState: Two nearly identical 680+ line components with same props interface, same CAPACITY_OPTIONS, same handler functions (handleSearchChange, handleTypeChange, handleStatusChange, handleSortChange), and same debounced search logic
code_quality.proposedChange:
Move shared ListingsFilterBar to packages/ds/src/blocks/ListingsFilterBar.tsx with:
1. Core component with configurable features via props
2. App-specific customizations through composition pattern
3. Shared constants (CAPACITY_OPTIONS, TYPE_TABS, etc.) in packages/ds/src/blocks/listings-filter/constants.ts
4. useListingsFilter hook for reusable filter logic
code_quality.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - extract common logic into reusable components in shared packages
prerequisites: Audit both components for subtle differences that need to be configurable

code_quality.title: Remove 231 console.log statements from production code
code_quality.description: Found 231 console.log/warn/error/debug statements across 30 files in apps/, with heavy concentration in critical modules: auth.controller.ts (42 occurrences), idporten.controller.ts (45 occurrences), main.ts (32 occurrences). These debug statements pollute production logs, risk exposing sensitive data, and indicate incomplete debugging cleanup.
code_quality.rationale: Console statements in production code are a code smell indicating incomplete development cleanup. They can expose sensitive information (tokens, credentials, user data), clutter production logs making real issues harder to find, and impact performance. The API module's auth controllers are particularly concerning as they may log authentication tokens.
code_quality.currentState: 231 console statements scattered across 30 files, particularly concentrated in authentication modules (87+ in auth-related files)
code_quality.proposedChange:
1. Replace all console.log with structured logging using pino (already configured)
2. Add ESLint rule to ban console.* in production code
3. Create debug utility that respects environment:
   - apps/api: use existing pino logger with appropriate log levels
   - apps/*: create debug utility that only logs in development
4. Review auth module logs for sensitive data exposure
code_quality.bestPractice: Use structured logging in production - never console.log. Sensitive data should never be logged.
prerequisites: Verify pino logger is properly configured across all API modules
Audit auth module logs for sensitive data before removal

code_quality.title: Add unit test coverage to apps/minside (currently 0 tests)
code_quality.description: The apps/minside application has zero unit test files, while apps/web has 4 tests and apps/backoffice has 14+ test files covering calendar, rental objects, and critical features. This gap leaves minside's user-facing features completely untested.
code_quality.rationale: apps/minside is the user portal handling critical user journeys: booking management, profile settings, notifications, GDPR compliance, and payment. Without tests, regressions can ship to production undetected. The settings.tsx (879 lines) and messages.tsx (916 lines) routes are particularly complex and need coverage.
code_quality.currentState: 0 test files in apps/minside, compared to 14+ in apps/backoffice and 4 in apps/web
code_quality.proposedChange:
Add critical test coverage:
1. apps/minside/src/hooks/useAuth.test.ts - Auth hook tests
2. apps/minside/src/routes/settings.test.tsx - Settings page tests
3. apps/minside/src/routes/bookings.test.tsx - Booking list/detail tests
4. apps/minside/src/features/listings/components/list/ListingsFilterBar.test.tsx
5. apps/minside/src/routes/messages.test.tsx - Messaging tests

Prioritize: Auth flows, booking management, GDPR consent handling
code_quality.bestPractice: Critical user-facing applications should have minimum 70% test coverage on business logic and UI components
prerequisites: Set up Vitest configuration for apps/minside if not present

code_quality.title: Split settings.tsx route files (1267 lines in backoffice, 879 lines in minside)
code_quality.description: The settings.tsx route files in both backoffice and minside have grown into monolithic components handling multiple unrelated settings domains. The backoffice version (1,267 lines) manages 7+ different settings tabs inline with complex form state management across profile, addresses, general settings, booking settings, notifications, integrations, and branding.
code_quality.rationale: Large route files violate single responsibility and make testing difficult. Each tab in settings.tsx handles different data models, has separate form validation, and makes different API calls. The 12+ useState hooks and inline form handlers indicate the need for decomposition into focused components with custom hooks.
code_quality.currentState:
Single massive route components with:
- 12+ useState hooks for form state
- 7 tabs rendered inline (100-200 lines each)
- Integration modal with inline handler (28 lines)
- Mixed mutation handlers and UI code
code_quality.proposedChange:
Extract each tab into dedicated component:

backoffice/src/routes/settings/
├── SettingsPage.tsx (orchestrator, ~100 lines)
├── tabs/
│   ├── ProfileTab.tsx
│   ├── AddressesTab.tsx
│   ├── GeneralTab.tsx
│   ├── BookingTab.tsx
│   ├── NotificationsTab.tsx
│   ├── IntegrationsTab.tsx
│   └── BrandingTab.tsx
├── hooks/
│   ├── useProfileForm.ts
│   ├── useTenantSettings.ts
│   └── useIntegrationSettings.ts
└── components/
    └── IntegrationConfigModal.tsx
code_quality.bestPractice: Route components should be thin orchestrators. Extract forms, complex UI, and business logic into focused child components and hooks.
prerequisites: Document current form behavior for each tab
Identify shared form patterns that can become hooks

topPriorities: Extract duplicated ListingsFilterBar - preventing inconsistent behavior
Remove console.log from production - security/logging concern
